themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 10 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 2.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 321% increase—suggesting a potential sanitation, pest, or environmental health issue requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 10 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.84)
Indicates potential cluster in a specific neighborhood area
reporting_angles: Investigate what's causing the cluster—disease outbreak, food contamination, pest control failure, or environmental contamination
Interview DSNY and NYC Health Department about response protocol and whether they've identified a cause

themes_detail.label: Homeless Assistance Spike
themes_detail.summary: Complaints requesting homeless person assistance surged to 4 THIS WEEK compared to 0.6 weekly average—a 540% spike—indicating either a concentration of unhoused individuals or a new shelter-related issue in the district.
evidence: 4 homeless assistance complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.85)
Community Board has repeatedly requested improvements to homeless shelter safety (recurring budget request)
reporting_angles: Map the 4 complaints—are they clustered near a specific shelter or transit hub?
Interview homeless service providers and NYPD about what triggered the sudden spike this week
Connect to long-standing community board concern about shelter safety and conditions

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints exploded to 59 LAST WEEK—a 442% increase over the 8-week average of 10.9 complaints per week (z-score: 8.18)—the highest z-score spike in the district data, signaling a major quality-of-life disruption.
evidence: 59 noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 10.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.18—highest severity spike)
442% increase; accompanied by 1100% spike in illegal fireworks (3 last week vs. 0.2 avg)
Also linked to 900% spike in bike/roller/skate complaints (5 last week vs. 0.5 avg) and 500% traffic complaints (9 vs. 1.5 avg)
reporting_angles: Investigate whether illegal fireworks, street racing, or organized bike/skating events caused the multi-category noise surge last week
Interview NYPD 106th Precinct about enforcement and whether they responded to the spike
Determine if the spike was incident-specific (event, construction) or reflects a new pattern

themes_detail.label: Building Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use violations spiked to 182 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO—a 331% increase over the 8-week average of 42.2 (z-score: 4.34)—paired with 312 DOB permits filed in the last 90 days, suggesting either construction code violations or a cluster of problem properties.
evidence: 182 building/use complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 42.2 weekly average (z-score: 4.34)
312 DOB permits filed over last 90 days (199 alterations), suggesting high construction activity and potential code violations
Community Board requesting additional DOB inspector capacity (recurring budget request)
reporting_angles: Identify which properties or blocks generated the spike in complaints 2 weeks ago
Cross-reference DOB permits with violation complaints to assess whether new construction is triggering code issues
Interview DOB about staffing and whether they can keep pace with permit volume and complaint investigation

themes_detail.label: Traffic and Cycling Disorder
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints surged 500% to 9 LAST WEEK (vs. 1.5 weekly average) while bike/roller/skate complaints jumped 900% to 5 (vs. 0.5 avg)—a convergence suggesting organized street activity, unsafe riding, or a traffic safety incident.
evidence: Traffic complaints: 9 LAST WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.3)
Bike/roller/skate complaints: 5 LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 6.36)
Concurrent with 442% street noise spike, suggesting possible street takeover or large cycling event
reporting_angles: Determine if the spike reflects organized street cycling events, street racing, or general traffic chaos
Interview NYPD about traffic enforcement response and whether they documented specific incidents
Check with community groups and social media for evidence of planned events or grassroots organizing
